purpose: A trip packing checklist: tap emoji preset chips (essentials/beach/camping/business/kids/international/winter) to bulk-add items, name the trip, add custom items, check them off as they hit the bag, then share the list by link or QR, print it, or "Uncheck all" to reuse the same list next trip — state persists in localStorage under key `packing-list` and travels in a base64url URL hash.
structure: Single scrolling page, no router, no tabs. `div.wrap` (index.html:781) is the only container — there is NO `<main>` element. Inside: `header.app` (782-787: decorative icon.svg, `h1` "Packing List", `span.spacer`, `a#tipLink.tipbtn.hidden` unhidden by JS). Then three `section.card` panels: (1) `.card.noprint` 789-793 — bare `input#tripName` with no label, `h2` "Start from a preset (tap to add)" carrying an inline `margin-top:12px`, and empty `div.chips#presets` filled by JS; (2) `.card` 795-805 — `h2#listHead` (text replaced at runtime by the trip name), `div.fillbar.noprint > div#fill` progress bar, `div.sub.noprint#fillText` counter, empty `ul.plain#list` filled by JS, `p.hint#emptyHint` acting as the de-facto empty state, and `div.row.noprint` holding `input#customItem` + `button#addBtn.btn`; (3) `.card.noprint` 807-815 — a `div.row` of four identical `.btn`s (uncheckBtn, shareBtn, qrBtn, printBtn) and a `p.hint`. Outside `.wrap`: `div#toast[role=status][aria-live=polite]` (818), `footer.colophon` (819), and `dialog#qrDlg` (821-825) containing an inline-styled `h3`, `canvas#qrCanvas` at a hardcoded 300x300, and `button#qrClose.btn`. Flow: land cold → tap preset chips → optionally name trip → add customs → check off → share/QR/print → "Uncheck all" to reset for the next trip. A `#`-hash on load decodes a shared list and, if the user already has items, gates the overwrite behind a native `confirm()` (app.js:130), then strips the hash via `history.replaceState`. The `<style>` block (17-778) is a generated SWS Studio base layer spliced between `▼▼▼`/`▲▲▲` markers (18/758) with a small app layer below the `APP LAYER` marker (760-777).

dynamicMarkup:
All list and preset content is built at runtime by `el()` (app.js:9-23), which sets `class` via `n.className = v` — a plain overwrite, so any class a restyle wants on these nodes must be added in JS, not CSS.

**Preset chips** — `renderPresets()` (app.js:51-63) clears `#presets` with `replaceChildren()` and appends one `<button class="chip" type="button">` per key of `PRESETS`, text from `PRESET_LABELS` (emoji + word, e.g. "🏖️ Beach"). No `.on`/selected state is ever applied, no `aria-pressed`, no wrapper element. Click merges the preset and toasts.

**Item rows** — `renderList()` (app.js:65-84) clears `#list` and appends, per item:
`<li class="done|">` → `<label>` containing `<input type="checkbox">` (checked set as a property, not an attribute) followed by a bare text node of `item.label`; then a sibling `<button class="x noprint" type="button" aria-label="Remove {label}">✕</button>`.
Critical couplings: the `done` class on the `<li>` (empty string when not done) drives `ul.plain li.done label`; the item text is an unwrapped text node with **no element around it**, so a restyle cannot target the label text separately without changing app.js:80; the checkbox is a **direct child** of the `<label>`, which is what makes the base `label:has(> input[type=checkbox])` 44px min-height rule match — wrapping the input in a span silently drops the row to ~36px.

**Other runtime mutations:** `#emptyHint` gets `.hidden` toggled (app.js:69); `#fill` gets `style.width` set as an inline percentage (app.js:70) so CSS cannot control it; `#fillText` textContent becomes "🎉 All packed!" or "N packed · N to go" or "" (app.js:71-73); `#listHead` textContent is overwritten with the trip name or "Your list" (app.js:74, 90); `#toast` gets textContent + `.show` add/remove on a 2400ms timer (app.js:25-31); `#tipLink` has `.hidden` removed and href set (app.js:120-124); `#qrCanvas` is painted imperatively with a hardcoded `size = 300` (app.js:151-166).

The whole list re-renders on every single interaction (check, add, delete, preset merge, uncheck-all), so any CSS transition or animation attached to `li`/`label` restarts from scratch each time — a restyle that adds row enter/exit animation will flicker the entire list on every checkbox tap.

The base's own token comment at line 148 says --t-micro is for 'uppercase labels only, never sentences'. `text-transform` also destroys the user's own capitalization ('Zoë's bachelorette' → 'ZOË'S BACHELORETTE').

Add a `.chip.tappable`/`.presetbtn` variant at `min-height:var(--tap)`, `padding:0 var(--s4)`, `font-size:var(--t-sm)`, `cursor:pointer`, with hover and `:active` states — or switch app.js:55 to emit `class: 'btn small'` with min-height raised.

comfortDefects.issue: Item labels — the actual content of the app — are set to `.98rem` (15.68px), and the base row rule underneath sets 15px. Both are under the 16px floor the design system explicitly promises in its own comment ('Body never drops below 16px … 14px body copy is the single most common reason a free tool feels cheap'). This is read at 6am in an airport, per the skin's own note at index.html:20.

comfortDefects.issue: The per-app skin's structural tokens are dead. `--r:16px` (line 26) and `--wrap:38rem` (line 27) are declared in the skin `:root`, then re-declared as `--r:14px` (line 166) and `--wrap:42rem` (line 182) in the base `:root` that follows. Equal specificity, later wins — so the app renders at 14px radius and a 672px measure instead of the intended 16px and 608px. Verified across all 23 apps: every index.html contains exactly 2 `--r` and 2 `--wrap` declarations, so the entire portfolio is rendering base defaults, not its skins.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:26-27 (skin) overridden by index.html:166 and :182 (base); source is design/studio.css:45 and :61, concatenated after the skin at design/build.mjs:366
comfortDefects.fix: Remove `--r` and `--wrap` from the `:root` block in design/studio.css (the skin generator already emits both for every app), then re-run `node design/build.mjs && node design/apply.mjs`. This one fix changes geometry across all 23 apps, so land it before any per-app tuning.

a11yDefects.issue: Both text inputs are completely unlabeled — no `<label>`, no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`. a11yDefects.issue: Placeholder text fails contrast at 3.34:1 — `--ink-3` #798e8c on `--field` #f6fcfc, against a 4.5:1 requirement. Because the placeholder is doing the labelling work, the app's entire naming mechanism is rendered in sub-threshold grey.

a11yDefects.fix: Darken light-mode `--ink-3` to roughly #5f7573 (≈4.6:1 on --field) or point `::placeholder` at `--ink-2` (#546866, 5.87:1). The dark palette already passes at 4.93:1, so this is a light-ramp fix in design/skins.mjs.

a11yDefects.issue: The footer and both its links fail contrast at 3.25:1 — `--ink-3` #798e8c on `--canvas` #eefaf9. The links are additionally forced to that colour by inline `style="color:inherit"`, so the Feedback mailto and the studio link are sub-threshold and colour-indistinguishable from surrounding text.

a11yDefects.issue: The QR dialog heading has a hardcoded `color:#111` inline. `<dialog>` defaults to `background-color:Canvas`, and `:root` declares `color-scheme:light dark`, so in dark mode the dialog paints a dark background under near-black text: 1.01:1 against Chrome's #121212 Canvas, 1.13:1 against Safari's #1e1e1e. The heading is effectively invisible in dark mode.

a11yDefects.issue: The progress bar is exposed to assistive tech as nothing at all — a bare `div` with an inline width, no `role="progressbar"`, no `aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax`, and no programmatic association with the `#fillText` counter that describes it.

a11yDefects.issue: Checking an item, deleting one, and merging a preset all trigger a full `renderList()` that silently replaces the list DOM. A keyboard user must re-tab from the top of the list for every item they check off — on a 30-item list that is unusable. This is a keyboard-operability failure, not a cosmetic one.
a11yDefects.where: app.js:77 (`onchange: () => { … renderList(); }`) combined with `list.replaceChildren()` at app.js:67

printSupport:
**Yes, print is a genuine supported path** — there is a dedicated Print button (index.html:812 → `window.print()` at app.js:114), the README frames the list as something you carry, and a paper checklist you tick with a pen is the natural fallback when your phone is in a bag. It is secondary to on-device checking off, but it is real, and it is currently the weakest surface in the app.

**Two print blocks exist and partially conflict.** Base: index.html:717-746. App layer: index.html:772-777.

**What works:** cards 1 and 3 carry `.noprint` so the trip-name field, presets, action buttons and add-row all drop out; `.fillbar` and `#fillText` are individually `.noprint`; the `.x` remove buttons get `noprint` from JS (app.js:81); `header.app`, `footer.colophon` and `#toast` are hidden; `@page{margin:14mm}` is set; `tr,li{break-inside:avoid}` keeps items from splitting across pages.

**What is broken or missing:**

1. **The printed sheet has no title.** `header.app` is hidden, so the only identifier left is `#listHead` — rendered as a 12px uppercase letterspaced grey eyebrow (base:349-357, with base print forcing `--ink-2:#333`). A packing list printed for a trip carries no legible trip name, no app name, and no date. Nothing uses `.printonly` (base:734), which exists for exactly this.

2. **Checked items may print identically to unchecked ones.** `ul.plain input[type=checkbox]{accent-color:#000}` (index.html:776) is largely inert: browsers suppress form-control backgrounds in print unless `print-color-adjust:exact` is set. The only surviving distinction is the `text-decoration:line-through` on `li.done label` (index.html:769), which does print — so the accent-color declaration is decorative and the intended checkbox fill will not appear.

3. **`break-inside:avoid` on the list card is a pagination hazard.** Base index.html:737-743 applies `break-inside:avoid; page-break-inside:avoid` to `section.card`. The list card holds the entire list, so a 30-40 item list asks the engine to avoid breaking a container taller than a page. Browsers degrade gracefully but it can force a near-empty first page. The app-layer rule at :775 overrides `border` and `padding` but not `break-inside`, so it stays live.

4. **`section.card{border:0; padding:4px 0}`** (index.html:775) overrides the base's `border:1px solid #bbb` (base:739), so the printed list has no frame and no visual separation from the page edge.

5. **The empty state prints.** `#emptyHint` is a `.hint` with no `.noprint`. The Print button guards on `items.length === 0` (app.js:113), but Ctrl/Cmd-P bypasses that guard entirely, so printing an empty list yields a page containing only the onboarding sentence.

6. **No multi-column layout.** A 40-item packing list prints as one narrow column down a full sheet, wasting most of the page. `columns:2` on `#list` inside `@media print` would halve the paper.

7. **No print-specific checkbox.** For a paper checklist the ideal is a generous empty square to tick with a pen; the current 20px `accent-color` input is a screen control carried into print unchanged.
riskyToRestyle: **QR canvas size is hardcoded in two places that must stay in sync.** `<canvas id="qrCanvas" width="300" height="300">` (index.html:823) and `const canvas = $('qrCanvas'), size = 300` (app.js:155). The module math — `cell = Math.floor(size / (count + 8))` (app.js:156) and `off = Math.floor((size - cell * count) / 2)` (app.js:157) — derives cell size and the quiet-zone offset from that literal. Changing the HTML attributes without changing app.js:155 draws the QR into the corner of a larger backing store or clips it. Style the canvas with CSS (`width:100%;height:auto`); leave the attributes and the literal alone.

**`.hidden` must keep `display:none !important`** (base index.html:691). JS toggles it on `#emptyHint` (app.js:69) and removes it from `#tipLink` (app.js:123). If the empty state is swapped for the `.empty` component, the new element must still carry `id="emptyHint"` and respond to `.hidden` — and `.empty`'s own `display` must not out-specify it.

**`#toast.show` is the entire visibility mechanism** (base index.html:641, driven by app.js:28 and :30). The toast is `opacity:0; visibility:hidden` by default; any restyle changing `#toast` display or transition must preserve the `.show` contract or every piece of feedback in the app goes silent.

**`li.done` is JS-applied as a raw className string** (app.js:79, `class: item.done ? 'done' : ''`) and is the sole hook for `ul.plain li.done label{text-decoration:line-through}` (index.html:769). Renaming it in CSS without editing app.js:79 removes the only visual indication that an item is packed — and, per the print findings, the only one that survives printing.

**`.x` and `.chip` are class names owned by JS**, not by markup: app.js:81 emits `class: 'x noprint'`, app.js:55 emits `class: 'chip'`, and `el()` sets them via `n.className = v` (app.js:13), a full overwrite. Renaming either in the stylesheet silently unstyles every remove button and every preset.

**The item label is an unwrapped text node.** `el('label', {}, cb, item.label)` (app.js:80) appends the checkbox then a bare text node. There is no element around the label text, so it cannot be targeted, truncated, or given its own type treatment without changing app.js:80 — and if you do wrap it, keep the `<input>` a *direct* child of the `<label>`.

**The 44px row height depends on a `:has()` rule the app layer only partially overrides.** Base `label:has(> input[type=checkbox]){min-height:var(--tap)}` (index.html:429-433) and app `ul.plain label{…}` (index.html:764-767) have identical specificity (0,1,2); the app rule wins on source order for the properties it declares but does NOT declare `min-height`, so the base 44px survives. Adding `min-height` to the app rule, or moving the checkbox out of direct-child position, collapses every row to ~36px.

**`#fill`'s width is owned by inline JS** (`$('fill').style.width = …`, app.js:70). No CSS rule can control it. If the progress bar is redesigned as a ring, a segmented meter, or anything not driven by a percentage width, app.js:70 must change with it.

**Inline `style` attributes will defeat new stylesheet rules on the same properties**: index.html:791 (`margin-top:12px`), :801 (`margin-top:10px`), :803 (`flex:0 0 auto` on `#addBtn`), :819 (`color:inherit` ×2), :821 (dialog border/radius/padding/text-align), :822 (h3 margin plus the dark-mode-breaking `color:#111`), :824 (wrapper margin). Lift these into the app layer first or the changes will appear to no-op.

**The `<style>` block between the markers at index.html:18 and index.html:758 is generated and will be overwritten.** `design/apply.mjs` splices between `▼▼▼ SWS STUDIO BASE` and `▲▲▲ END SWS STUDIO BASE` (apply.mjs:35-36). All hand edits belong below the `APP LAYER` marker at index.html:760; anything above it is lost on the next `node design/build.mjs && node design/apply.mjs`.

**The duplicate-token cascade must be fixed at source, not per app.** `--r` and `--wrap` are declared twice in every generated file (skin at index.html:26-27, base at :166 and :182) and the base wins. The base copies come from design/studio.css:45 and :61, concatenated after the skin at design/build.mjs:366. Verified across all 23 apps. Fixing it changes card radius and container width portfolio-wide in one step — land it first and re-baseline any screenshots rather than compensating per app.

**Service worker caching will pin the old design.** `sw.js:2` sets `VERSION = 'pack-v5'` and `sw.js:3` precaches `./index.html`, which is where all the CSS lives; the fetch handler is cache-first (`return cached || fetched`, sw.js:19), so returning visitors keep the old stylesheet until the version string changes. Bump `VERSION` as part of the restyle commit. **Not a risk:** test/helpers.test.mjs is pure logic — it imports only from helpers.js and asserts on data, with zero DOM, class-name or structure assertions — so markup and class names can be changed freely without touching tests.
